A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same FlexHook work, and all 11 pages of each are readable, including equations, figures, tables, and references. Neither contains an appendix or embedded supplement. Separate Supplementary Materials are mentioned but are not included in either supplied PDF.

before.justification: v4 reports original FlexHook benchmark results, component ablations, encoder-freezing experiments, and timing measurements in Tables 1 and 3–7.

after.justification: v5 retains the original FlexHook benchmark, ablation, encoder-freezing, and timing results in Tables 1 and 3–7.

M1.justification: Section 3 retains the same C-Hook sampling and conditioning, temporal integration, Pairwise Correspondence Decoder, and training losses. No algorithmic component or procedure changes.

E1.justification: Both evaluate the same coverage: Refer-KITTI, Refer-KITTI-V2, Refer-Dance, and LaMOT, including its TAO, SportsMOT, VisDrone, and MOT17 subsets.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 3 retain identical comparator membership within each benchmark. No baseline is added, removed, or replaced.

E3.justification: Section 4.1 retains the same split handling, detector–tracker combinations, evaluation metrics, input resolution, and training settings. The timing comparison protocol in Section 4.3.4 is also unchanged.

E4.justification: Tables 4, 6, and 7 retain the same analyses of C-Hook, PCD, temporal integration, conditioning-point counts, neighboring sampling, and encoder freezing. No ablation or robustness analysis is added or removed.

E5.justification: Both retain point-estimate reporting without reported repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: All result entries and reported findings are unchanged. For example, FlexHook-best retains HOTA scores of 53.83 on Refer-KITTI, 42.53 on Refer-KITTI-V2, 32.17 on Refer-Dance, and 56.77 on LaMOT.

T1.justification: The problem formulation, mathematical definitions, and Equations (1)–(4) are unchanged. No formal assumption, derivation, or proof is added or revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same claims about improving two-stage referring-by-tracking, reducing dependence on CLIP, and outperforming existing methods with greater efficiency.

C2.justification: Interpretations of conditional cues, tracking-noise robustness, and encoder-freezing tradeoffs remain unchanged. The discussion of LaMOT's TAO subset and other applicability qualifications is also retained.

D1.justification: The abstract replaces the statement that code is in the Supplementary Materials with a direct GitHub link to buptLwz/FlexHook. This changes code-access information; implementation details, hyperparameters, and hardware disclosures remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion and all 51 references are unchanged, as is the positioning relative to single-object tracking, one-stage RMOT, and iKUN.

P1.justification: The abstract's code-access sentence and the arXiv version/date notice change. The remaining prose, terminology, and section order are retained.

P2.justification: The repository link slightly lengthens the abstract, causing small column and page-break shifts across pages 1–3. Figures and tables retain their content and design; pages 4–11 render identically.

improvement.justification: v5 provides a specific code repository link where v4 only points to Supplementary Materials, modestly improving code discoverability. The scientific content and evidence are unchanged. The supplied PDFs do not establish the repository's availability or contents, so the supported benefit is limited to clearer access information.
